data.title: Reads after a write stay fast through compaction, not through an incremental projection
data.why: Measured on 10,000 events (KAD-48): the fold takes 3 ms, reading the files 171 ms; a read after a write took 211 ms, warm 36 ms. After compact: 28 ms and 5 ms. The cost is the disk, not the fold, so an apply(state, event) proven equivalent to project() would save 3 ms while putting I1 at risk. prime now names kadence compact once more than 5,000 events sit in loose files from earlier months, and the 566 ms in the task's description is from before KAD-45.
data.rejected: An incremental apply(state, event) for every event type: saves the 3 ms the fold costs, and needs proof of equivalence against project() in every read order; Caching every event inside state.json: every warm read would parse the whole journal again to save the read after a write; Compacting automatically after a write: rewrites files in the user's repository without being asked
